sub_scenario.one_line: documentary post-production editor: share a cleared packet before live selection

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the edit decision list and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The rights tracker review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I took notes in a routine edit review without losing context.
Was a rights replacement still open?
No, the cut and notes were already aligned.
Someone new shadowed me in the review room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the delivery weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.

For the archival-interview cut, I linked each removed line in the edit decision list to its rights status before sharing the change packet with the producer; the packet showed which replacements were cleared.
What did the producer receive?
A rights-linked handoff that connected every edit to its clearance record.
I joined a short live check when one sound cue needed clarification.
Did that approve replacement footage?
No, it settled a contained cue question.
I archived last cycle's notes on the rights tracker and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The morning producer review is at 10:00, and clearance counsel posts tracker updates in batches by 11:30.
Are those times fixed?
Yes, both are on the delivery-week schedule.
A vendor call about the edit decision list ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the review room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the delivery weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the rights tracker records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
In an earlier live review, the group restored a compelling clip that later proved restricted, requiring a weekend recut.
What was missing from the room?
The rights tracker had not yet recorded clearance for that replacement.
I sketched next week's plan for the delivery weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the edit decision list updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The rights-cleared packet can be sent on the review channel after counsel updates the tracker, and the roster reserves a ten-minute live slot only for competing cut versions.
Are both channels available?
Yes, the packet release and narrow live slot are on the approved form.
I compared two options for the rights tracker tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the review room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
What is the best way to move the archive sequence forward while counsel is finishing its review?

replacement_dialogue.content: I filed the routine delivery weeks paperwork and confirmed the owner list.
I did a standard pass over the rights tracker records this morning.

During a July archive review, I read the decision-list timestamps, tracked which tracker entries were still blank, and recorded producer questions; the clearance lead approved replacements after the tracker updated, and no clip was selected during my segment.
Did you restore restricted footage live?
No, I maintained the review record while the lead handled approval.
